title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
author: Eric Jorgenson
blurb: Eric Jorgenson gathered years of Naval Ravikant's tweets, podcast conversations and essays and organized them into one short guide. Naval is an entrepreneur and investor best known for cofounding AngelList. The book has two halves. The first is about wealth. Naval argues that getting rich is a learnable skill, not luck. It comes from owning assets, building specific knowledge that others can't easily copy, using leverage like code and media, and taking accountability for your work. The second half is about happiness. Naval treats happiness as a skill too, built through habits like meditation, reading, exercise and letting go of endless desire. The thread connecting both halves is freedom. Wealth buys freedom from having to work. Inner peace frees you from your own restless mind.

lessons.t: Getting rich is a skill, not luck
lessons.b: Seek wealth, meaning assets that earn while you sleep, rather than chasing a salary or status, because wealth creation is a positive-sum game anyone can learn.
Your edge is knowledge that can't be taught in a classroom, found by following your genuine curiosity toward work that feels like play to you but looks like work to others.

lessons.t: Use leverage that needs no permission
lessons.b: Code and media multiply your effort without anyone's permission, letting one person's work reach millions while they sleep.
